title: Utility Order for South Louisiana Electric Cooperative Association, ex parte. — Order No. U-37929 accepts the Joint Report for the 2025 Test Year Formula Rate Plan filing submitted on September 30, 2026, which states that an adjustment in rates for a revenue increase of $ 578,811 is necessary and in accordance with the terms of South Louisiana Electric Cooperative Association (“SLECA”) Formula Rate Plan. This matter was considered at the October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session.

documents.text:
LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                  ORDER NUMBER U-37929

    SOUTH LOUISIANA ELECTRIC COOPERATIVE ASSOCIATION, EX PARTE.

Docket No. U-37929, In re: Formula Rate Plan annual earnings monitoring report for test year
ending on December 31, 2025.

               (Decided at the October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


                                             ORDER

Overview and Procedural History

       The Louisiana Public Service Commission (“Commission”), having reviewed and
considered the Joint Report and Draft Order on South Louisiana Electric Cooperative
Association’s Formula Rate Plan Annual Report Filing for the Test Year Ending December 31,
2025 (“Joint Report”) submitted by the Louisiana Public Service Commission Staff (“Staff”) and
South Louisiana Electric Cooperative Association (“SLECA” or “Cooperative”), finds the Joint
Report, together with its attached exhibits, to be acceptable and in accordance with the provisions
of the Commission’s Order No. U-36339-A dated May 22, 2023, and Order No. U-36339-B dated
November 12, 2025, which established the Cooperative’s current Formula Rate Plan (“FRP”) for
test years 2023-2025. The Joint Report was filed into the record on September 30, 2026.
       The Joint Report indicated that, after adjustments, SLECA earned a Times Interest Earned
Ratio (“TIER”) that fell below the bandwidth prescribed in the Cooperative’s FRP and, therefore,
that the implementation of a rate increase of approximately $578,811, or 1.98%, in FRP Rider
revenue is required.


Commission Jurisdiction and Authority
       The Commission exercises jurisdiction over public utilities in Louisiana pursuant to Article
4, Section 21(B) of the Constitution of the State of Louisiana, which provides the following:
               The commission shall regulate all common carriers and public
               utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by law.
               It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations, and
               procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and shall have
               other powers and perform other duties as provided by law.

       Pursuant to its constitutional authority, the Commission issued Orders Nos. U-36339-A
and U-36339-B, which established SLECA’s current FRP. The Cooperative’s FRP provides for a
TIER bandwidth with a lower endpoint of 1.40, an upper endpoint of 1.60, and a midpoint of 1.50,
as well as a lower limit Modified Debt Service Coverage Ratio (“MDSC”) of 1.40. Under the FRP,
if a test year’s TIER is less than 1.40 or greater than 1.60, SLECA’s FRP Rider revenue is to be
increased or decreased, respectively, by the amount necessary to increase or decrease the TIER to
reach the midpoint of 1.50. Additionally, if a test year’s MDSC is less than the lower limit of 1.40,
SLECA’s FRP Rider revenue is to be increased by the amount necessary to increase the MDSC to
reach the lower limit of 1.40.



                                                                                Order No. U-37929
                                                                                           Page 1
 Commission Consideration
       After discussion, on motion of Vice Chairman Coussan, seconded by Commissioner
Campbell, with Commissioner Francis and Commission Lewis concurring, and Chairman
Skrmetta temporarily absent, the Commission voted to accept the Joint Report and issue the draft
order filed into the record on September 30, 2026.


THEREFORE, IT IS ORDERED THAT:
   1. The Commission accepts the Joint Report filed on September 30, 2026, and issues the Draft
       Order.
   2. SLECA is authorized to adjust its rates to generate an increase in base rates of
       approximately $578,811 to reach the midpoint TIER of 1.50, subject to the following
       conditions:
           a. Within thirty (30) days after the issuance of this Order, SLECA shall submit an
                updated and revised tariff reflecting the Commission’s action to the Commission’s
                Utilities Division and Legal Division for their review and approval. SLECA shall
                not implement the rates authorized by this Order unless and until Commission Staff
                receives and approves the Cooperative’s updated and revised tariff.
           b. This action is taken without prejudice to the Commission’s authority to make
                investigations and request any reasonably necessary change that the Commission
                may legally find to be in the public interest.
This order is effective immediately.

BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA
November 19, 2026
